 Form W-4V Withholds Federal Tax From Your Social Security Check and Nothing for Your State. Retirees in the Eight States That Still Tax Benefits Find Out When the State Return Asks for the Whole Year at Once
 Vilma Rios Fri, November 13, 2026 at 10:27 AM CST 5 min read Quick Read 
 Form W-4V withholds only federal tax from Social Security, so retirees in eight states face a lump-sum state bill and interest in April. 
 A hypothetical Connecticut couple with $130,000 in IRA withdrawals owes about $6,579 in state tax, yet Social Security accounts for only about $529. 
 Connecticut charges 1% monthly interest on missed installments, but withholding from a December IRA withdrawal counts as paid evenly all year.

 Picture a retired Connecticut couple in their 70s sitting down in April 2027 with their 2026 returns. The federal return goes smoothly. Years ago they filed Form W-4V, so Social Security has taken federal tax out of every check, but the IRS side still shows a balance due of about $10,321. 
 Highwaystarz-Photography / Getty Images Then the Connecticut return requires for roughly $6,579 in one payment. It also adds interest because they didn't pay in quarterly pieces during the year. Nobody withheld anything for the state, because Form W-4V only talks to the IRS. 
 The couple is an hypothetical example, but the trap is real in the eight states that still tax benefits in 2026: Colorado, Connecticut, Minnesota, Montana, New Mexico, Rhode Island, Utah and Vermont. West Virginia left the list this year after fully exempting Social Security benefits. 
 Form W-4V Has Only Federal Boxes 
 Social Security lets you withhold 7%, 10%, 12%, or 22% of your monthly payment for federal income tax. The form has no line for state tax, and the agency's withholding options cover only the IRS.

 On the federal side, Section 86 of the Internal Revenue Code taxes up to 85% of the social security benefits received. That kicks in once half your benefits plus all your other income, including tax-exempt interest, passes a base amount. The base for married couples is $32,000. The states follow their own rules on their own calendar, and your Social Security check never goes toward them. 
 Story Continues How a Connecticut Couple Ends Up Owing $6,579 
 Here are the assumptions for tax year 2026. The couple files jointly. They collect a combined $3,208 a month, which is the SSA's estimated average for an aged couple after the 2.8% 2026 COLA. That works out to $38,496 a year. They also take $130,000 in traditional IRA withdrawals and have no other income. 
 Their federal provisional income comes to $149,248, so 85% of their benefits, or $32,721.60, is federally taxable. A 12% W-4V election takes $384.96 a month, about $4,619.52 over the year, and every dollar of it goes to the IRS. 
 Connecticut taxes joint filers with federal AGI of one hundred thousand dollars or more on no more than 25% of their benefits, which here is $9,624. The state's new full deduction for IRA withdrawals covers only joint filers with federal AGI less than one hundred fifty thousand dollars. This couple's federal AGI is $162,721.60, so they miss it. Their $24,000 personal exemption shrinks by $1,000 for every $1,000 of income above $48,000, which leaves nothing at their income. 
 Connecticut 2026 line 
 Amount

 $139,624 
 Tax from joint rate schedule ($4,000 plus 5.5% above $100,000) 
 $6,179.32

 Total Connecticut tax

 The rates come from Conn. Gen. Stat. § 12-700(a)(10)(C). Social Security's own share of the bill is about $529. The rest comes from IRA withdrawals that also had no state withholding, because the couple never requires for it. Connecticut exempts benefits entirely below the AGI lines of $75,000 for single filers and $100,000 for married couples. Each of the other seven states uses its own thresholds. 
 Connecticut's Interest Clock Runs Every Quarter 
 Connecticut requires four estimated installments, due on the fifteenth day of the fourth, sixth and ninth months of the year and January 15 of the next year. Each installment you underpay gets interest at one per cent per month or fraction thereof. 
 Say each installment is a quarter of the bill, or $1,644.83, and the couple pays nothing until April 15, 2027. Interest then runs for 12, 10, 7 and 3 months on the four installments, adding about $526. That brings the total to roughly $7,106. You owe no interest if your tax after withholding is less than one thousand dollars, or if you owed no Connecticut tax the year before. The math above assumes their 2025 return looked similar. 
 Three Moves That Shrink the April State Bill 
 Have state tax withheld from IRA withdrawals. Connecticut handles withholding as if it were goes an equal part on each due date. One large withholding from a December IRA withdrawal therefore counts as if you goes evenly all year. In Connecticut the withholding form for pension and IRA payers is Form CT-W4P. 
 Send quarterly estimates. Mail Form CT-1040ES on the four due dates. Each one should be a quarter of what you requires to owe. 
 File early if you missed the fall payments. If you file and pay in full by January thirty-first, Connecticut drops the interest on the fourth installment. 
 A tax professional can help you choose between withholding and estimates while you plan your IRA withdrawals for the year.
